messages:
alex: quick follow-up to the shrink vs async-evictor RFC we merged — we still haven't landed the actual allocator-facing contract for shrink hints vs explicit eviction requests. i sketched something, want quick reactions before i open the cleanup PR.

maria: depends what problem we want to optimize for. is the primary concern latency spikes from synchronous shrink or memory compaction effectiveness?

alex: both. in practice synchronous shrink blocks inference threads and causes p99 spikes; async evictor + advisory shrink hints reduces p99 but can increase fragmentation if the evictor can't keep up.

chris: my take: keep small, simple allocator API. two calls: `advise_shrink(range_id, weight)` which is advisory, and `request_eviction(range_id, min_pages)` which queues a high-priority task. allocator never blocks callers on eviction.

sara: +1 on non-blocking. also we need a way to wire backpressure into the request path — e.g. if evictor queue is saturated return a lightweight rejection so caller can fallback to a lower-memory config.

ben: prototype sketch:
```
// allocator.h
bool advise_shrink(RangeId r, int weight); // best-effort
EvictToken request_eviction(RangeId r, int min_pages); // returns token or null if overloaded
// EvictToken.status() -> ready/queued/failed
```
if token == null caller can set `X-Prefer-Sync-Shrink: true` or demote batch size.

alex: i like the EvictToken idea because it decouples lifecycle. chris — do you envision tokens as heavy-weight (futures) or just ids that can be polled?

chris: lightweight ids + poll/callback. future/async wrapper in runtime layer for convenience. don't expose futures deep in hot paths.

maria: question about ordering/races: allocator might observe a shrink hint, then immediately hand allocation to host-staging which races with evictor doing async compaction. need clear state transitions in the contract.

sara: agreed. propose states: idle -> hinted -> pending_eviction -> reclaimed. allocator should provide `query_residency(range_id)` that returns a coarse residency state so callers can make decisions. keep it intentionally coarse to avoid contention.

ben: telemetry note: add `evict_queue_length`, `avg_eviction_latency`, `shrink_hit_rate` metrics. we'll correlate with p99 inference latency.

alex: about the fragmentation risk: what if evictor gives up because it can't find contiguous pages? we should expose a `force_compact(range_id)` admin path (higher CPU cost) that can be rate-limited.

chris: `force_compact` should be gated behind quota and admin flag, yes. maybe only allowed for Dedicated deployments by default.

maria: operational concern: Private/VPC customers may want synchronous shrink for compliance reasons (deterministic memory reclaim). so we need a config flag `allocator.sync_shrink_policy = {always, advisory, on_demand}`. default = advisory.

alex: ok that's reasonable. i'll include config knob in the PR. also adding an internal flag `--evictor-max-inflight` and `--evictor-queue-threshold` to control when tokens are refused.

ben: small nit — make token refusal explicit response code so SDKs can retry with reduced batch sizes. e.g. `ERR_EVICTOR_OVERLOADED`.

alex: good. i'll draft the PR with API sketches + sequence diagrams showing the race windows. will also add a short migration guide for callers: how to degrade to smaller batches when token refused.

deploy-bot: PR #4489 opened by alex: "allocator: add advisory shrink + evict token API, config knobs, metrics" — https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/4489 :shipit:

chris: i'll review. one last thought — consider TTL-based post-eviction compaction to amortize compaction cost across tenants. maybe a follow-up RFC.

alex: noted. thanks all. i'll tag you on the draft and try to keep the runtime wrappers thin.

sara: thanks — landing this should help p99 a lot. also add a short test harness that simulates sustained evictor saturation so we can validate the fallback behaviors.

alex: will do, thanks :thumbsup:
